title: Separate module mode, gradient mode and first-use policy caching
applies_when: A PyTorch layer selects a training or inference path from grad mode, module training state or input shape, or initializes a persistent policy during its first forward. A warmup temporarily changes backend compile mode while separately caching a group's initialization status.
lesson: Module train/eval state and autograd recording are independent. Read the real caller and the implementation's supported modes before selecting an inference fast path. Check every dispatch, including optional branches, with supported train/eval and grad/no-grad controls. Also test transitions: no-grad or inference-mode warmup followed by grad-enabled training. A temporary no-grad policy must not silently become the permanent training policy; preserve explicit policies and verify normal policy reuse. Native outputs and gradients establish the scoped behavior, not only a mocked selected-mode assertion. For failed warmup, inspect both temporary backend mode and persistent readiness: restoring one does not repair the other. DeepGEMM's original warmup leaves compile mode at 1 on executor failure and retains its early initialized marker on lock/allocation/synchronization failure. Restore the saved mode on exceptional exit, clear only the failed group's marker, re-raise the original error and exercise a same-key retry. Retain successful-group caching, other keys and older backends without both mode APIs. Distinguish the early reservation from successful completion instead of moving it blindly and changing reentrancy behavior.
avoid_when: Do not impose a universal chunk-mode requirement: another recurrent implementation may support training, and a caller may legitimately restrict mode combinations. Do not unconditionally clear an explicit or already-valid cached policy. Small layer and checkpoint tests do not qualify full-model training, compiler capture, other dtypes or accelerators, measured memory-budget satisfaction or performance. Matching gradients within existing numerical checks is not necessarily bitwise identity. The DeepGEMM evidence is registered Linux CPU state tests with mocked GPU/executor boundaries, not native kernels, safe recovery from a corrupted CUDA context, concurrent warmup correctness or a performance result. This development repair does not establish prospective evidence-selector utility or maintainer acceptance.

evidence.note: PyTorch documents eval/train as independent of no-grad and inference modes. This explains the distinction, not a verdict about a particular dispatch.
This baseline's shared branch selects fused_recurrent for short no-grad inputs before asserting training requires chunk; its top-level dispatch already checks not self.training.

Merged correction. Six real RTX5090/float32 layer cases produced two short shared-memory training failures before and six passes after; dependent tests had 238 passes and eight existing skips. Twelve ordinary training/eval comparisons matched outputs and gradients within the existing numerical check. This does not qualify skipped full-model tests.

Open, unmerged correction for the deprecated public selective checkpoint wrapper. Current-main no-grad/inference-mode warmup caches [] and bypasses later budget optimization. The committed fix passes five CPU lifecycle/explicit-policy controls plus three real CUDA/SciPy solver cases at budgets 0, 0.5 and 1, comparing outputs and input/parameter gradients on Torch 2.11/RTX5090. CPU lifecycle tests mock only the optimizer. No measured memory or speedup claim.

Proposed two-layer cleanup retains the early per-group reservation, removes that marker only on unsuccessful warmup and restores the saved compile mode in finally. Symmetric-memory restoration and legacy API guards remain. Public fork source, not an upstream merge.

Seven source-package registered CPU regressions have six failure results before and all pass after the repair on Linux CPython3.12; the existing meta-tensor warmup-memory test also passes. Tests cover interruption, allocation/mode-entry/synchronization/lock failure, same-key retry, successful caching and partial/absent mode APIs. Windows function-body component controls pass on CPython3.12/3.14. These are scoped state results, not GPU or official CI qualification.
